Version 0.3.3 adds per-peer outbound delivery status to the Ratatui dashboard. The selected folder shows queued file versions, logical bytes and metadata records using each transfer lane's durable acknowledgements. Offline peers, incomplete lanes, pending scans and conflicts remain distinct states. “Indexed changes delivered” confirms outbound reconciliation; it does not certify that the remote scanner is idle or that remote conflicts are resolved.

Queue sampling runs in one background worker with bounded work, caches unchanged results, and skips entry queries once all lanes reach the local revision. Large queues show a lower bound when the counting budget expires. Queued sizes are before delta/resume savings, not predicted network traffic. The monitor continues to read only daemon snapshots for its dashboard.

Native user-service lifecycle tests now run on Ubuntu and macOS: login enablement, clean restart, automatic crash recovery, offline edits, reverse replication, permissions, symlinks, deletions, retained originals and cleanup. A local macOS trial passed 12 restart cycles, including four forced crashes. Actual machine reboot/logout testing and longer stability trials remain open. Delta-efficiency tests now publish complete edits atomically and separately cover visible truncation and recovery.

**Wire protocol 5 is unchanged and remains compatible with 0.3.2.** Upgrade with `brew update && brew upgrade ysync`, then restart the service and reopen the monitor to use the new dashboard. Cargo users can install tag `v0.3.3`. Identities, configuration, indexed history, conflict records and resumable transfers are retained. Experimental prerelease.
